messages.subject: Getting Labels Not To Sort
parts:
Hello:

I am having issues with the labels on ggplot - they are sorting in
alphbetical order. However, when I change them to numeric, then the
scale gets thrown off because the scale is discrete.

When I run this code, the x axis disappears.
pG<-qplot(as.numeric(rownames(dag)),dag[,1], geom="bar",
stat="identity")
pG<-pG + xlab(paste(paste(paste(paste("Average Days of Delay for -
",'',inn),' ( Respondent Count',dcc),' of ',tcc),'',")"))
pG<-pG + ylab(paste("Count of \n Responses for \n - ",'',rll)) +
opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5, size = 8)) +
opts(axis.title.y = theme_text(angle = 90, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5,
size = 8))
pG<-pG +
scale_x_discrete(breaks=c(2,3,4,5,7.5,10),labels=c(2,3,4,5,7.5,10))
pG<-pG + opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size=8,
colour="black",vjust=1))+ opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size=8,
colour="black", hjust=1))

When I do not turn the rownames into numeric, then the 10 comes before
the 2.

Any suggestions?

Kai

messages.author: 599a13812d4cd3e8
messages.subject: Re: Getting Labels Not To Sort
parts:
Would be a lot easier to answer if you provided some test data ... but either convert the variable to a factor, with the order specified in the levels argument, or provide the order you want to the limits argument in scale_x_discrete. See the thread earlier today ("Legend Question") where Hadley and I were talking about this.

Hmmmm, it might be as simple as changing scale_x_discrete to scale_x_continuous (since that's what would be used after the numeric conversion). Again if you provide data we can, you know, answer more easily :)

--J
